question: Can bounded projection-constrained direct coefficient edits preserve native prior public-state/action predictions exactly while learning new identifiable public action consequences from later observations, without an oracle family label or hidden source state?
hypothesis: In authored two-regime linear development where old observations span 8 of 10 public action-context feature directions (s3=0) and later observations reveal changes confined to the two previously unused s3/sign(action)*s3 directions, a fixed-rank projection repair will retain old public predictions (max drift <=1e-9), fit novel observed-state consequences (new VALID RMSE <=0.03), and match independently solved constrained batch ridge (max forecast gap <=1e-8), while an unedited base has larger new VALID RMSE by >=0.05. This is a narrow subspace adaptation hypothesis, not proof of unknown causal-family discovery.
